note: City of Bayfield campground 1 mi north of downtown, in heavy woods on the slope above Lake Superior facing Madeline Island. A walkway runs from the campground road toward the lake, and there are lookout points over the Apostle Islands. Nearest dump station is the wastewater plant south of town, by appointment on weekdays; showers at the Bayfield Recreation Center for a fee. --Claude
summary: City page, 2025 brochure + site map, imagery (Esri, NAIP) and street map read. Fees $30 confirmed (2026 page); FCFS only confirmed; season mid-May - mid-Oct confirmed (closed Oct 19 2026); electric 30, no water/sewer confirmed; 34 sites, 25-ft recommendation confirmed; showers false and dump false added. LAKEVIEW not supported from the sites (continuous canopy, ~100 m+ from shore); lead: coastal walk (Lake Superior, own walkway, no highway between). Pin is the entrance at Hwy 13 (~170 m off).
flags: WATERFRONT lead lakeview -> coastal walk. Lake Superior. The city's street-map park polygon runs from Hwy 13 down to the shore; the campground road (Dalrymple Park Rd) runs NE parallel to the shore about 100-150 m inland, and the brochure map shows a 'Walkway' from the road by site 22 toward the lake, with sites 21, 22, 24 and 26 on the lake side of the road. No highway, town, rail line or residences between the sites and the shore. Esri and NAIP show continuous leaf-on canopy over the whole campground, so no site can be placed on open ground or shown to see the lake: a lakeview from the sites is unsupported ('overlooking Lake Superior' is the city's marketing; the brochure photo of a bench over the lake is a lookout, not a site). Per the coastal-walk rule (Great Lake, any setting, own park ground between, no sightline needed) this fits coastal walk; if the reviewer reads the walkway as only reaching a bluff lookout rather than the shore, the fallback is not waterfront. Suggested waterfront_evidence: 'City brochure map + Esri/NAIP + street map 2026-11-16: wooded sites ~100-150 m from Lake Superior on the city park's own ground, walkway from the road by site 22 toward the lake, no highway/town between; canopy hides the sites -> coastal walk'.

Pin 46.8186,-90.8098 sits at the entrance on Hwy 13; the campground road's middle is about 46.8190,-90.8077, ~170 m east (optional move, under 250 m). The schematic site map can't place individual sites on imagery.
Rig length: the city 'don't recommend RVs larger than 25 feet' - a 23-ft rig is within it. Wooded, rustic sites.
